::: {#fig-stationary-point-3d fig-alt="Surface plot of x1 squared plus x2 squared minus 2 x1 over x1 from -1 to 3 and x2 from -2 to 2, a bowl-shaped surface opening upward.
The lowest point of the bowl, at (1, 0) and height -1, is marked by a vermilion circle and is the stationary point.
A vermilion diamond marks the point of the surface above the origin, at height 0, where the surface is not flat."}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: stationary-point-3d-r
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| eval: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
sp3_x1_3d <- seq(-1, 3, length.out = 101)
sp3_x2_3d <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 101)
sp3_f_3d <- function(x1, x2) x1^2 + x2^2 - 2 * x1
sp3_z_3d <- outer(sp3_x2_3d, sp3_x1_3d, sp3_f_3d)
sp3_x1_marks_3d <- c(1, 0)
sp3_x2_marks_3d <- c(0, 0)
sp3_z_marks_3d <- sp3_f_3d(sp3_x1_marks_3d, sp3_x2_marks_3d)
sp3_kind_3d <- c("stationary point", "not stationary")
sp3_symbol_3d <- c("circle", "diamond")
sp3_marks_3d <- tibble::tibble(
  x1 = sp3_x1_marks_3d,
  x2 = sp3_x2_marks_3d,
  z = sp3_z_marks_3d,
  kind = sp3_kind_3d,
  symbol = sp3_symbol_3d
)
sp3_marker_3d <- list(color = "#D55E00", size = 6, symbol = ~symbol)
plotly::plot_ly() |>
  plotly::add_surface(
    x = sp3_x1_3d,
    y = sp3_x2_3d,
    z = sp3_z_3d,
    colorscale = list(c(0, 1), c("#CCE0F0", "#0072B2")),
    showscale = FALSE,
    opacity = 0.8
  ) |>
  plotly::add_markers(
    data = sp3_marks_3d,
    x = ~x1,
    y = ~x2,
    z = ~z,
    text = ~kind,
    hoverinfo = "text",
    showlegend = FALSE,
    marker = sp3_marker_3d
  ) |>
  plotly::layout(
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "x1"),
      yaxis = list(title = "x2"),
      zaxis = list(title = "f(x)"),
      camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.6, y = -1.6, z = 0.9))
    ),
    legend = list(orientation = "h")
  )
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: stationary-point-3d-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Surface plot of x1 squared plus x2 squared minus 2 x1 over x1 from -1 to
#|   3 and x2 from -2 to 2, a bowl-shaped surface opening upward. The lowest
#|   point of the bowl, at (1, 0) and height -1, is marked by a vermilion
#|   circle and is the stationary point. A vermilion diamond marks the point
#|   of the surface above the origin, at height 0, where the surface is not
#|   flat.
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

sp_x1_3d = np.linspace(-1, 3, 101)
sp_x2_3d = np.linspace(-2, 2, 101)
sp_x1_grid_3d, sp_x2_grid_3d = np.meshgrid(sp_x1_3d, sp_x2_3d)
sp_value_3d = sp_x1_grid_3d**2 + sp_x2_grid_3d**2 - 2 * sp_x1_grid_3d
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4.5))
ax = fig.add_subplot(projection="3d")
ax.plot_surface(sp_x1_grid_3d, sp_x2_grid_3d, sp_value_3d,
                color="#0072B2", alpha=0.6)
ax.scatter([1], [0], [-1], marker="o", color="#D55E00", s=50,
           label="stationary point")
ax.scatter([0], [0], [0], marker="D", color="#D55E00", s=50,
           label="not stationary")
ax.set_xlabel("x1")
ax.set_ylabel("x2")
ax.set_zlabel("f(x)")
ax.legend(loc="upper right")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [graph](functions.qmd#def-graph) of the [function](functions.qmd#def-function) of @exm-stationary-point,
the surface whose [level curves](vector-calculus.qmd#def-level-curve) are in @fig-stationary-point.
The surface is flat, with [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative) $\vzero$, only at the bottom of the bowl above the center $(1, 0)$ of the circles,
the [stationary point](#def-stationary-point) (circle).
Above the origin (diamond) the surface slopes downward toward the stationary point.

:::
